ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Referral — Ulysses S. Grant — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Primary care visit for four weeks of right-sided throat pain and painful swallowing in a heavy cigar smoker

text.paragraph: Please evaluate and advise on nicotine dependence, other tobacco product, uncomplicated and dysphagia, oropharyngeal phase and abnormal weight loss. [S]
Urgent otolaryngology–head and neck surgery referral for a persistent right tonsillar lesion with painful swallowing in a heavy cigar smoker, for laryngoscopy and biopsy within two weeks. [S]
Referral for the concerns below, which began before the index visit. [S]

list.item: Right-sided throat pain for four weeks, worse with swallowing, that has not improved. [S]
Wants a clear answer about the diagnosis quickly so he can plan for his family and finish his memoir. [S]
Has smoked cigars most of his life and is unsure he can stop. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Hiram Ulysses Grant was born on April 27, 1822, in Point Pleasant, Ohio, the first child of Jesse and Hannah Grant. [D]
Grant was a heavy cigar smoker: his tobacco use rose during the Civil War to about eighteen to twenty cigars a day, and he reported smoking nine or ten a day in peacetime. [D]
In June 1884, at his summer home in Long Branch, New Jersey, Grant began to have stinging throat pain and pain on swallowing. [D]
Grant had recurrent severe, incapacitating headaches, interpreted retrospectively as most likely migraines. [R]
In 1858 Grant had fever and chills, possibly from malaria or typhoid, and he had periodic fevers believed to have been malaria. [R]
Grant's father, Jesse Grant, died in 1873 at age 79; his mother, Hannah Grant, died in 1883. [D]

text.paragraph: 7 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.

Order a contrast-enhanced CT of the neck before the specialist visit, and PET/CT for staging once biopsy confirms carcinoma. Guideline: NCCN Guidelines Insights: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2025 (2025) [S]

Tobacco cessation: advise stopping cigars, set a quit date, behavioral counseling at every visit, and varenicline. Guideline: Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions (2021) [S]

Nutrition: dietitian assessment before treatment, a soft calorie-dense diet with oral supplements, and a weight at every visit; the head and neck team decides on a feeding tube if weight loss nears 10%. Guideline: NCCN Guidelines Insights: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2025 (2025) [S]
Dental evaluation and fluoride care before radiation to the neck. Guideline: NCCN Guidelines Insights: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2025 (2025) [S]

Symptom control with liquid acetaminophen and topical lidocaine, pain scored at each visit, and escalation by the oncology team during treatment. Guideline: NCCN Guidelines Insights: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2025 (2025) [S]

Check CBC, basic metabolic panel, and albumin before and after treatment; baseline TSH before neck radiation, repeated every six to twelve months afterward. Guideline: NCCN Guidelines Insights: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2025 (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression and hypothyroidism monographs (2026) [S]
Screen for depression with the PHQ-2 at each primary care visit after the diagnosis. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression and hypothyroidism monographs (2026) [S]
